label: Where the Views Sit
title: Two questions, not one line
intro: The creation debate is often drawn as one line from young earth to evolution. It is really two questions: how old the earth is, and whether all life shares common ancestors. Each view is placed by its own statement.
image_title: Creation and science: two questions, not one line
image_subtitle: How old is the earth, and does all life share common ancestors?
image_subtitle_narrow: How old is the earth, and does all life share common ancestors?
caption: Three evangelical views on two separate questions. Old earth creation and evolutionary creation agree on the age of the earth and part ways on common descent. No major view pairs a young earth with common descent, so that corner is empty.

positions.name: Young earth creation
positions.placement: Thousands of years; common descent rejected
positions.text: Six consecutive 24-hour days and a recent creation. God made the original kinds, and Adam and Eve, directly.
positions.short_text: Six 24-hour days, a recent creation, the kinds made directly.

positions.name: Old earth creation
positions.placement: Billions of years; common descent rejected
positions.text: The creation days are long periods and the earth is billions of years old. God created new forms of life directly, humanity as a special creation.
positions.short_text: Long creation days, billions of years, new life forms made directly.

positions.name: Evolutionary creation
positions.placement: Billions of years; common descent accepted
positions.text: God created through evolution over billions of years. All life on earth is related, humans included, which does not negate the image of God.
positions.short_text: God created through evolution; all life, humans included, is related.

differ: Age: six 24-hour days and a recent creation (Answers in Genesis), or billions of years (Reasons to Believe and BioLogos).
Common descent: Answers in Genesis and Reasons to Believe hold that God created kinds or new forms of life directly; BioLogos accepts that all life, humans included, is related.
Adam and Eve: Answers in Genesis and Reasons to Believe hold they were the first two humans, made directly. BioLogos says evolutionary creationists differ; some hold they were a historical couple.

Scripture and science: Answers in Genesis calls old earth and evolutionary readings incompatible with Scripture. Reasons to Believe and BioLogos hold that Scripture and nature, rightly read, do not conflict.
common_text: All three confess God as the Creator of all things and the Bible as his inspired word. BioLogos puts the common ground this way: "While Christians differ on their views of the age of the earth and evolution, we all agree on the essentials of the faith."
note: No view is presented here as the answer.
image_source: Sources: Answers in Genesis, Statement of Faith; Reasons to Believe, FAQ; BioLogos, What is Evolutionary Creation?

sources.title: Statement of Faith
sources.quote: The days in Genesis do not correspond to geologic ages but are six consecutive, 24-hour days of creation
sources.notes: Also: 'Scripture teaches a recent origin of man and the whole creation, with history spanning approximately 4,000 years from creation to Christ.' 'The various original life forms (kinds), including mankind, were made by direct, supernatural, creative acts of God (i.e., not by natural, physical processes over millions of years).' 'Adam and Eve did not originate from any other preexisting lifeforms.' It names progressive creation, day-age, framework hypothesis and theistic evolution (i.e., evolutionary creation) among views 'incompatible with Scripture'.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.quote: Does RTB believe the earth is billions of years old? Yes.
sources.notes: Also: 'We believe God directly intervened in history to create new forms of life, with humanity as a special creation in his image.' 'RTB understands the creation “days” in Genesis as long periods of time.' On evolution: RTB accepts 'some limited change (microevolution)' and rejects 'the idea that all life' arose from macroevolution.

sources.title: Statement of Faith
sources.quote: Adam and Eve, the first human beings, chose to rebel against God and go their own autonomous way.
sources.notes: Also: 'Properly understood, God’s Word (Scripture) and God’s world (nature), as two revelations (one verbal, one physical) from the same God, will never contradict each other.'

sources.title: What is Evolutionary Creation?
sources.quote: We therefore accept the scientific evidence that all life on Earth is related, including humans
sources.notes: Also: EC 'takes the Bible seriously as the inspired and authoritative word of God'; 'ECs generally agree that people were made by God and that humans are biologically related to other creatures'; 'Some ECs believe Adam and Eve were a historical couple.' biologos.org answers scripts with a bot challenge (HTTP 429); read in headless Chrome.

sources.title: What does the fossil record show?
sources.notes: Full sentence: 'The oldest fossils, microbial mats in Greenland, are 3.7 billion years old!' Read in headless Chrome.

sources.title: How is BioLogos different from Evolutionism, Intelligent Design, and Creationism?
sources.quote: While Christians differ on their views of the age of the earth and evolution, we all agree on the essentials of the faith
